contents.entry: The line-ops audit: what counts, from which records
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
What this volume needs from the shared volumes

pointers.sibling: Input and output record schema of this node
Build-mode flag, whose state the verdict records
Tier promotion, whose break glass counts as a hand operation
pointers.shared: Product work frozen until the exit test passes (D19)
The line operations a seat never performs and how seat.result reports attempts
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: Once a day, decides from records whether the line ran itself: zero agent line operations, zero hand line operations, a clean owner checkout at origin/main, every merged PR holding only its ticket's declared files, and at least one ticket moving cut to verified; passes lift the product freeze (D19 B) by one record.
purpose.is-not: It is not a human review of the day and it is not a status report; N-28 turns the verdict into one card on the first pass and on every third consecutive fail; the Stats screen shows the daily rows.
purpose.why: ROADMAP Phase 2 done-when: a day of running leaves git status clean and every pull request holds only its ticket's files (ROADMAP.md:134), not met on 2026-10-14 (L05 section 5 item 5); D19 B: frozen to infrastructure until a named exit test passes, with the test written into the design.

input.record: The daily tick at 00:05Z; the day under test is the previous UTC day 00:00:00Z to 23:59:59Z.
Every verified 201 and rejected 422 record of the day (main verdicts).
input.query: Line-ops audit rows (section audit) from the day's records; git status --porcelain and rev-parse of the owner checkout, read with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; the day's merge records with their PR file lists versus the tickets' declared files.

output.record: Pass: every criterion row true; the day; the counts; freeze.state off is written in the same transaction with the verdict id as its reason.
Fail: the failing rows with evidence (record ids, the git status lines, the PR and the extra files); the consecutive fail count.
Not run: the line did nothing that day (no ticket moved cut to verified), so there is nothing to judge; the freeze stays; not a fail.
off (on a pass) with the verdict id; on (initial, written at bring-up by the system lane from the D19 ruling, and again if the owner rules the freeze back on).
output.reads: N-28 (card on the first pass: product work may resume; card on every third consecutive fail with the top failing row), N-03 (accepts tickets with lane product only while freeze.state is off), N-40 (daily rows), N-33 (the rail's R-09 and R-10 rows read the pass).

audit.row: Count of records of a line-op kind (merge, verify, promotion, cleanup.run, dispatch, lease, cancel, branch.delete, ticket.request from a cleanup, seat start or stop) whose by field is a seat id instead of a node id. The seat deny list (N-13) makes these impossible to run, and N-01 refuses a put of a line-op kind from a seat with 403, so the count is of refused puts plus any that slipped, and both must be 0.

Sum of seat.result.denied_line_ops over the day's seat results (a seat tried make serve, git push to main, gh pr merge, systemctl, cleanup.sh, and was denied). Over 0 is a brief defect to fix, shown on the Stats screen; it does not fail the day.

Records with origin break-glass or by owner on a line-op kind (N-42 control.action of kind break-glass, N-48 promote.sh by hand, N-45 cleanup.sh by hand, N-49 unlanded.sh by hand, a Reload by hand), plus reflog entries in the owner checkout of the day not made by the fast-forward of N-49 step 3 (reflog lines whose message is not merge --ff-only origin/main).

git status --porcelain in the owner checkout is empty (tracked and untracked) and HEAD equals origin/main at the tick; a known-dirty exception list is not allowed after N-49 step 3 is done; before that, the three known files of 04-UNLANDED section 7 are the only allowed lines and the row says so.

row.name: PR files equal declared files
row.must: true for every merge of the day

audit.row: For every merge record, the PR's changed file list (from forge.snapshot) is a subset of the ticket's declared files plus the generated aggregates the ticket's node volume allows; an extra file names the PR and the file.

row.name: at least one cut to verified

audit.row: Tickets whose ticket.ready, dispatch, pr.opened, merge and verified 201 records all fall in the day or earlier with the verified in the day.

row.name: no dead tickets created by a line defect

audit.row: dead records of the day with reason class line (stall of a system node, 503 from a system node) are listed; over 0 is reported on the card as context; they do not fail the day because the owner's criterion is operations, not failures.
The build-mode.state and hold flag state at the tick, for the record; a pass under build mode on is a pass (build mode governs old rules, not the exit criteria).

mechanism.where: Go package exittest in the service; the git reads use the service's own git with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 against the owner checkout path from config (read-only; the service never writes there except N-49's fast-forward).
mechanism.step: On the daily tick, take lease exittest:<day>; query the store for the day's records by kind and by; compute rows A1 to A8.
Run git status --porcelain and git rev-parse HEAD and origin/main in the owner checkout; read the reflog for the day.
For every merge of the day, read the PR file list from the forge snapshot at the merge sha and the ticket's declared files from the ticket record; compare.
Decide: A6 equals 0 gives 204; any of A1, A3, A4, A5 failing gives 422; else 201 and freeze.state off in the same put batch (N-01 multi-record put with one idempotency key exittest:<day>).
Keep the consecutive fail counter in the verdict; N-28 reads it.

diagram.mermaid: flowchart TD T[daily tick 00:05Z] --> Q[query day's records: line-op kinds, seat results, merges, verified] Q --> G[git status, HEAD vs origin/main, reflog of the owner checkout] G --> F[PR files vs declared files per merge] F --> D{A6 > 0?} D -- no --> N[exit.verdict 204 not run] D -- yes --> E{A1 A3 A4 A5 all pass?} E -- no --> X[exit.verdict 422 rows + consecutive count] E -- yes --> P[exit.verdict 201 + freeze.state off] P --> C[N-28: one card, product may resume]

start.s: The daily tick starts it; the records it reads are written by the nodes as they run; no one collects evidence by hand and no one declares the exit test passed in prose.
The freeze itself is a record the system lane writes at bring-up from the D19 ruling; N-03 enforces it on intake; nobody reminds anyone.

wait.fallback: one retry; then exit.verdict 503 reason store and an alert; the next daily tick covers two days (the day field is a range)

wait.what: git reads in the owner checkout
wait.fallback: a lock or a missing checkout gives A4 false with the reason; the verdict is 422 with that row, because an unreadable checkout is not a clean checkout

wait.what: forge file lists for the day's merges
wait.fallback: N-04 ladder; then A5 is false with reason unreadable for that PR; the verdict is 422 and the next day re-checks the same merges if they are still in the window (the window is the day, so a persistent forge outage fails days, which is correct)
another instance holds it (cannot happen under N-06's single unit); skip; idempotency key makes a double run harmless

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human judging whether the day was clean. The rows are computed from records and git, and the freeze flips on the record.

retries.policy: Store and git reads inside one run.
retries.recover: After three failures: exit.verdict 503 for the day; the freeze is unchanged; the next tick runs for the next day and includes the failed day in its range.
retries.report: 201 is one card the first time and a counter after; 422 is a Stats row and one card every third consecutive fail with the top row; 204 is a row only; 503 is an alert record.

many-agents.readers: Every seat is subject to the audit and none reads it to behave; the seat contract's deny list is what makes A1 zero, and the audit is the proof, so twenty seats running at once add rows to A2 at most.
many-agents.writers: One verdict per day under one idempotency key; a re-run returns the first record; the freeze flip is in the same batch, so a crash between verdict and flip cannot leave them apart.
many-agents.collision: A seat writing a record at 23:59:59Z and the tick at 00:05Z: the window is by record at, assigned by N-01 at commit, so a late put lands in the day it committed; the five-minute offset lets the last records commit.

The owner editing the checkout at the tick moment: A4 reads what is there; a dirty checkout at 00:05Z fails the day, which is the rule (the checkout is the owner's working surface only through tickets after N-49 step 3).
Two merges of the same ticket on one day (a fix after a rejected main): both are checked in A5 against the same declared files; both must hold.

freeze.state off and a product ticket cut in the same second: N-03 reads the flag at validation; an earlier put is refused 412 frozen and the ticket request is re-validated on the next tick, so no product ticket is lost and none slips through early.

status-codes.emits: Pass; owner reads one card the first time; system lifts the freeze.
Fail; system acts (fix tickets from the rows where a node is named); owner reads a card every third consecutive fail.
Could not compute; system acts (alert, next day range).
on or off; N-03 acts on intake.

state-paths.path: The full row evidence per day (the record carries a bounded copy).
Generated from verified records for the plan's R-09 proof; the owner's artifact.

edges.in: verified 201 and rejected 422 of the day
edges.out: freeze.state to N-03 by store read (not drawn: N-03 reads flags at validation)

item.check: A clean day passes and lifts the freeze in one batch.
item.proof: A test world with one ticket cut to verified by system actors only, a clean checkout fake and matching PR files; exit.verdict 201 and freeze.state off with the same key; N-03 then accepts a product ticket.

item.check: A seat's refused line-op put is counted in A1 and fails the day.
item.proof: A test put of kind merge by a seat id; N-01 refuses 403; the verdict is 422 with row A1 naming the record.

item.check: A hand promotion fails the day.
item.proof: A promote.sh run with origin break-glass recorded; row A3 names it; 422.

item.check: An untracked file in the checkout fails the day.
item.proof: A fake checkout with one untracked file; row A4 lists the line; 422.

item.check: A PR with an undeclared file fails the day.
item.proof: A merge whose file list has one extra path; row A5 names PR and path; 422.

item.check: A day with no movement is 204, not a fail, and does not reset the consecutive count.
item.proof: A test world with no records of the day; 204; the counter unchanged.

item.check: The consecutive fail counter reaches 3 and posts one card.
item.proof: Three failing days on the fake clock; one card record from N-28 keyed on day three.

item.check: R-09's proof is generated from records.
item.proof: Ten consecutive verified tickets with no stall record between them produce R-09-ten-tickets.tsv with ten rows.

may.do: read the day's records; read the owner checkout; write exit.verdict and freeze.state
rule the freeze back on (a ruling record), or lift it early by a ruling that names the reason (recorded as freeze.state off reason owner-ruling, and the card says the test did not pass)

may-not.do: write exit.verdict or freeze.state; write a product-lane ticket while the freeze is on; perform any line operation
declare the exit test passed in prose or a ledger row; the record is the only pass

monitoring.counter: A1 over time; any non-zero is an alert.
A2 over time; the brief defect signal.
monitoring.panel: One row per day with the eight rows as lamps; the Rail's R-09 row reads ten consecutive verified tickets from the same records.

runbook.step: A seat wrote or tried to write a line-op record: the seat contract's deny list has a hole; the fix ticket request names N-13 and the kind.
A hand operation happened (break glass or a hand git in the checkout); it is the owner's own; nothing to fix unless it was an agent, which is A1.

Read the lines; an untracked runtime file means a writer still targets the repository (a fix ticket for that writer); a modified tracked file means a hand edit (the owner's; it goes through a ticket).
The named PR carried a file its ticket did not declare; N-14's claim check or N-18's validator missed it; the fix ticket names the node.

step.when: the owner wants product work before a pass

runbook.step: A ruling lifts the freeze with a reason; the card says the test did not pass; D19's intent is recorded as overridden by the owner, which is the owner's right.
runbook.cleanup: line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry N-51.rows, N-51.log; N-51.proof by owner disposition.
runbook.cold-start: Verdicts are in the store; the next tick computes the next day; a missed day is included in the range.

sources.source: Phase 2 done-when: a day of running leaves git status clean and every pull request holds only its ticket's files; Phase 3: a ticket goes from cut to verified with zero architect prompts
D19 B with the exit test written into the design
D19 ruled: frozen until a day with zero agent line operations and a clean checkout
Item 5: the main checkout is permanently dirty; the Phase 2 exit test is not met; a clean checkout is what the starter needs
Agents doing line operations (43 of 92 hand merges, 66 of 66 hand verifies) and status as a file on a branch
D11: code does the mechanical jobs; agents write, judge and rule
R-05 proof: no agent or human action between cut and merged; R-09: ten consecutive tickets without a stall
V07 one file one in-flight ticket (the A5 row), V08 probes not opinions
The three known dirty files allowed until N-49 step 3
Monitoring is the system reporting on itself

reject.source: the architect ticking the roadmap's done-when box by hand (ROADMAP.md, How the architect follows this)
reject.reason: A prose pass is an opinion; the verdict is a record computed from records and git.

reject.source: D19 option A (product resumes at the first slice) and C (a product lane now)
counting idle minutes or agent activity as the criterion
reject.reason: D17: the idle alarm is retired; the criterion is operations and a clean checkout, not busyness.

reject.source: failing the day on dead tickets (A7)
reject.reason: The owner's criterion is that the line runs itself, not that every ticket succeeds; dead tickets are the line's output and are reported, not counted against the day.

reject.source: reading the seats' transcripts for line operations
reject.reason: State from transcripts is on the kill list (L15 section 9 item 2); the deny list and the refused puts are the evidence.

shared-needs.need: principles.xml#product-frozen (D19) with the eight audit rows named as the test.

seat-contract.xml#line-ops: the list of line-op commands denied to every seat; seat.result carries denied_line_ops (count and the command names); a seat put of a line-op kind is refused 403 by N-01 and counted.
flags row freeze (state, reason, verdict_id); exit_verdicts: day, code, rows JSON, consecutive_fails; a query by kind and by over an at range.

exit.verdict, freeze.state, the line-op kind list (merge, verified, promotion, cleanup.run, dispatch, lease, cancel, branch.delete, seat.start, seat.stop, reload.request), control.action with origin break-glass, seat.result with denied_line_ops.
201 pass, 422 fail, 204 not run, 503 could not compute; 403 for a seat put of a line-op kind; 412 frozen on a product intake.
Multi-record put under one idempotency key (verdict plus freeze flip); the at field assigned at commit.
Intake refuses lane product with 412 while freeze is on; re-validates on the next tick.
forge.snapshot carries each PR's changed file list at merge.
Card rules: first 201 once; 422 every third consecutive; card text templates.
exittest.owner_checkout, exittest.tick 00:05Z, exittest.known_dirty_files (until N-49 step 3 done), exittest.card_every_fails 3.
